note:
Measured across all three Quantization Profiles on CPU and CUDA, over the twelve
committed Port Validation Cases of each Reference Model Variant. Numerical
acceptance thresholds and perceptual quality evaluation remain deferred; no
placeholder tolerance or quality score is claimed.

This file previously carried an empty `stages` object with the measurements
described only in prose. That was not a formatting detail. Because
tests/python/test_tolerance_coverage.py skips families with no recorded grid,
this family had no cross-check between what the package claims and what was
actually run, and on 2026-07-26 that let a real defect ship silently: removing
the CUDA strict-FP32 gate changed duration.w_ceil on the 315-token case, moving
the frame count by one hop, and nothing failed. It was found by comparing CPU
against CUDA by hand.

Both Reference Model Variants are recorded, under `variants`. Keying the file on
family alone was the second half of the same hole: vits-vctk has its own twelve
cases and its own speaker-conditioned path, so a grid that is full for
vits-ljspeech says nothing about it. The coverage test now checks each variant
against its own reference profile, and that was verified to bite by deleting a
stage from each variant in turn and watching it fail.

The structural probes are the guarantee that has to hold across backends, and
they hold on both variants: duration.w_ceil, duration.y_length and
duration.attention are exact on every case, every profile and both backends.
That is not free -- the stage producing them runs on CPU on every backend, for
the reason recorded in docs/porting/families/vits.md. The duration-path slice
reports no worst-case drift because there is none to rank: its probes are
integers compared for equality, so its entries carry exact_on_every_case rather
than a measured maximum.

One limit remains, stated rather than implied. CUDA drift is measured against the
CPU oracle while CUDA F32 matrix multiplies compute at TF32 precision, so the
intermediate figures mix implementation difference with precision difference; see
docs/backends.md.
